description: Find the resource id of ONE person or ONE location by name — `type` is REQUIRED and must be "person" or "location"; 10 best matches; NAME search only (no code or id lookup). This is the id source for assign_item, adjust_stock, transfer_stock, set_min_stock, create_order (deliverToResourceId), create_item (homeLocationId) and create_location / create_person (parent). A "person" here is a PERSON RECORD — someone items can be assigned to — NOT a login account; member userIds come from list_members. Every row carries `path`, the ancestor names root→parent ("Schulhaus B" → "1. Obergeschoss" for a room, a department chain for a person), plus `parentId`: when several locations share that name, the path is what tells them apart — read it out to your user and let them pick instead of writing against a guess. An empty result [] means no match — retry with the most distinctive word, or browse the whole tree with list_resources (which also answers "what rooms do we have?" and "who is in the organization?" — this tool needs a name to search for and returns nothing for an empty query).
name: search_resources

result.description: Up to 10 best name matches; empty array means no match

parentId.description: The parent resource's id (absent at the top level) — what create_location / create_person take as `parentId`

path.description: Ancestor NAMES, root→parent (e.g. ["Schulhaus B", "1. Obergeschoss"]); empty at the top level. When several rows share a name, this is what tells them apart — read it out and let your user pick instead of guessing

title: Search people & locations
